claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 13 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 13 years old.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are specific circumstances where you may still be eligible for Child Benefit.

Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you working as a Crown servant (for example, for the UK diplomatic service or armed forces posted overseas)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living overseas, but I'm not working as a Crown servant - I don't work for the diplomatic service or armed forces or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. 

Since you're living abroad and you're not a Crown servant, your eligibility would depend on which specific country you're living in. According to the rules, you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries.

Could you tell me which country you're currently living in? This will help me determine if Child Benefit can be paid to you there.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country, but it's just a regular country - nothing special about it in terms of UK agreements or anything like that. Does that make a difference for whether I can claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, I'm afraid that does make a difference. 

Based on the rules for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK to qualify. The exceptions are:

1. If you live in certain specific countries that have agreements with the UK
2. If you're a Crown servant working abroad

Since you've indicated that:
- You're living abroad in a country without special UK agreements
- You're not a Crown servant

Unfortunately, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex while living abroad in these circumstances.

Just to confirm I have all the details correct: Alex is your 13-year-old son, you live with him abroad, and you're not in the UK or working as a Crown servant. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - Alex doesn't live with me. He lives in the UK, not abroad. I'm the one living abroad, but he's still back in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important clarification. So Alex lives in the UK while you're living abroad.

To determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about Alex's living situation and your involvement in his care.

Who does Alex live with in the UK? And are you contributing financially towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me since I'm abroad. I do contribute financially towards his upkeep - I help with things like clothes, school expenses, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you're contributing to Alex's upkeep with things like clothes and school expenses.

To determine if you can claim Child Benefit, I need to know:

1. Who specifically does Alex live with in the UK? (For example, is it your partner, a relative, a friend, or someone else?)

2. How much do you contribute towards his upkeep? Specifically, is it at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, or about £111 per month)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Alex lives with his other parent in the UK. 

As for how much I contribute, yes, I do contribute at least that amount - I send about £26 a week to help with his expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details.

So to summarize:
- Alex (13 years old) lives in the UK with his other parent
- You live abroad (not as a Crown servant)
- You contribute about £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep

I have one more important question: Is Alex's other parent (the one he lives with in the UK) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his other parent isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Nobody else is getting it for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one final question to complete my assessment:

You mentioned you contribute about £26 per week. Are you making these contributions regularly (weekly, monthly, or in lump sums), and have you been doing so consistently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I send the money regularly - I make sure to send it every week consistently.

**Key Issue: UK Residency Requirement**

The fundamental rule for Child Benefit is that you normally qualify if:
- You're responsible for a child under 16, AND
- **You live in the UK**

While it's positive that:
- Alex is 13 years old (under 16) ✓
- You're contributing regularly to his upkeep (£26 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit amount) ✓
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex ✓

The main problem is that **you live abroad and don't meet any of the exceptions** that would allow you to claim while living outside the UK. Those exceptions are:
1. Living in certain specific countries with UK agreements 
2. Being a Crown servant (diplomatic service, armed forces posted overseas, etc.)

Since you've indicated you don't fall into either category, you don't meet the residency requirement.

**What could happen:** Alex's other parent, who lives with him in the UK, would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex if they wished to do so, as they meet the residency requirement and live with the child.

I hope this explanation is clear. Please let me know if you have any questions.
